chunks: My father (peace be upon him) and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Sa‘īd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about voluntary prayer during Taqsīr (shortening) at the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), the sites of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the two Ḥarams. He replied, 'Yes, perform voluntary prayers as much as you are able.'

key_terms.نُقَصِّرُ: We shorten (referring to Taqsīr of prayers)

ai.seo_question: Can one perform voluntary prayers while shortening obligatory prayers at holy shrines?
ai.summary: This narration from Imām al-Ṣādiq (AS) clarifies that the concession of Taqsīr does not preclude the performance of voluntary prayers, affirming the spiritual richness of Ziyārah as a time for both obligatory for brevity in obligatory acts but open to abundance in voluntary ones. It highlights the distinct jurisprudential status of the shrines of the Ahl al-Bayt and the two Sanctuaries as places where the pilgrim is encouraged to maximize devotion without the constraint of the travel-shortening rule. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that Ziyārah is not merely a ritual visit but a comprehensive act of worship where voluntary prayers serve as a means of drawing closer to the Imams.
